messages.content: "Can you help me find a book? I'm not sure of the title, but I know it's a mystery novel. I'd like to search in the library in New York City first, then I'd like to check Google Books and Open Library. Can you assist with these searches?"

function.name: google_books_search
function.description: Search for a book in the Google Books library with optional parameters Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

title.description: Title of the book. Default is not use it if not specified.

function.name: library_search_books
function.description: Search for a book in a given library with optional parameters Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

title.description: Title of the book. Default is not use it if not specified.

function.name: openlibrary_books_search
function.description: Search for a book in the Open Library with optional parameters Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

title.description: Title of the book. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to perform three searches:

1) Search in a library located in NYC (New York City). They want a mystery genre.

2) Then search on Google Books for same criteria.

3) Then search on Open Library.

We need to call each tool accordingly. The order matters: "search in the library in New York City first". So we should do library_search_books with location="New York City", genre="mystery".

Then google_books_search with genre="mystery".

Then openlibrary_books_search with genre="mystery".

But note that the function signatures require at least genre; title optional. We don't have title. We'll just pass empty string maybe? But they say default is not used if unspecified. So we can omit title param entirely.

Thus calls:

First: library_search_books({"location":"New York City","genre":"Mystery"}).

Second: google_books_search({"genre":"Mystery"}).

Third: openlibrary_books_search({"genre":"Mystery"}).

We'll produce results from each. Let's proceed.
